summary: The paper proposes delaying the choice of sparse storage until compile time, so that a compiler can select and transform the data structures of matrices annotated as sparse in dense source code. It reports preliminary timings for LU factorisation, a tridiagonal solver and sparse loop nests on an HP-UX 9000/720 machine and one Cray CPU.
why_read: Read it as an example of compile-time sparse data-structure selection, noting that its only distributed-memory content is one sentence in the introduction.
main_contribution: A compile-time method that encapsulates sparsity guards and expands access patterns, then selects and transforms sparse storage while resolving conflicts between access patterns.
main_limitation: Conflicts between access patterns cannot in general be resolved, and the experiments are preliminary timings on one HP-UX 9000/720 machine and one Cray CPU.
evaluation_method: preliminary timings on one HP-UX 9000/720 machine and one Cray CPU, plus code comparisons with a hand-coded tridiagonal solver and SPARK
benchmarks: LU factorisation of D(n,5) matrices (n = 200 to 500)
four Harwell-Boeing matrices in Table 4 (row, column and reshaped variants)
SPARK hand-coded row and column codes (qualitative)
